description: Saving a detail edit (decision 23): the new settings apply from today as a dated version. Same-day edits replace today's version, an edit back to the previous settings removes it, unchanged settings add nothing (weekdays, month days and dates compare as sets; phones write weekdays Monday first and the rest ascending), and more than 100 versions fold the oldest into the next. Structural edits never come here: they end the goal and start a new one.

today.description: The effective practice day of the edit.

cases.description: Changing the target on 12 October adds a version from that day; the past keeps its target.
A second edit on the same day replaces that day's version instead of adding another.
Editing back to the previous version's settings on the same day removes today's version.
Saving the settings unchanged (for example only the name or a pause changed) adds no version.
An edit on the day the goal was created replaces its first version, keeping its from.
When the last version starts after today (written by a device whose day is ahead), the edit replaces it and keeps its from.
Changing the end (until 31 December) is a detail edit like any other: a version from today.
Weekdays, month days and dates are sets: the same days in another order are no change, so no version is added.
The 101st version folds the oldest into the next: the first version goes and the second takes its from, so the cap of 100 holds.
